name: Barbell Snatch
summary: An Olympic weightlifting movement in which a barbell is lifted from the floor to an overhead lockout in one continuous, explosive motion caught in a full squat.

setup: Stand with feet hip-width apart and midfoot directly under the barbell.
Grip the bar with a wide snatch grip using a hook grip, fingers wrapped over the thumbs.
Lower your hips, keep your chest upright, retract your shoulder blades, and ensure your shoulders are slightly ahead of the bar with back flat.
steps: Initiate the first pull by pushing the floor away through the whole foot, keeping the torso angle constant until the bar passes the knees.
Accelerate into the second pull as the bar reaches mid-thigh, violently extending hips, knees, and ankles while shrugging the shoulders upward.
Pull yourself aggressively under the barbell as it reaches maximum elevation, transitioning your feet outward into a squat stance.
Receive the bar overhead with locked elbows in a deep overhead squat position.
Stabilize the weight in the bottom position, then stand fully upright by driving through the heels until hips and knees are locked.
instructions.breathing: Take a deep breath and brace the core tightly before initiating the pull from the floor; hold the brace through the catch, exhaling as you stand to completion.
cues: Punch the ceiling in the catch

common_faults.fault: Swinging the barbell outward in a loop away from the body during the pull.
common_faults.correction: Keep elbows high and outside during the turnover, brushing the bar close against the thighs and hips.

common_faults.fault: Soft or unlocked elbows upon catching the bar overhead (pressing out).
common_faults.correction: Punch aggressively upward into the barbell and lock out the arms before absorbing the weight into the squat.

common_faults.fault: Hips rising faster than the shoulders off the floor.
common_faults.correction: Maintain a consistent torso angle during the first pull by driving through the legs rather than lifting with the back.

precautions: Use bumper plates on a dedicated lifting platform to allow safe bailing of missed attempts.
Practice dumping the barbell forward and backward safely before handling heavy loads.
Do not use lifting straps during maximal competition-style lifts where an overhead bailout might be necessary.
